summary: Santa Cruz County enclosed-tower lookout listed gone; an environmental notice describes the site as an existing CAL FIRE communications facility, where a 60-foot wood pole burned in 2020.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the enclosed tower as Gone; an environmental notice describes the site as an existing CAL FIRE communications facility

access.note: Inside a CAL FIRE lease area in Big Basin Redwoods State Park. The sources describe a communications site, not a public lookout.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE)

events.note: Division of Forestry photo captioned Chalks Lookout, taken October 28, 1953; the archive note says it is believed to show the former Eagle Rock lookout instead
The existing 60-foot wood pole at the site burned in the CZU August Lightning Complex fire; a 35-foot emergency repeater was then temporarily installed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Unresolved. The archive caption says Chalks Lookout, but its note says the photo is believed to show the former Eagle Rock lookout. The story flags the doubt and does not describe the lookout's appearance from this photo.

notes_for_editor: No source read gives a build date, a builder, a staffing history, or the date the lookout tower came down. The weebly Chalk Mountain page has only its heading, so it was not cited. The 2023 construction start in the CEQA notice is a plan; the story says the sources do not show it was done. The site facts (an existing CAL FIRE communications facility, the 2020 pole fire, the Big Basin lease area) rest on two agency or consultant documents and are consistent with each other. The FFLA gone status is the only source for the lookout's removal. Confidence is low because the lookout's own history is essentially missing from the sources read.
